name: Canada (federal)
appliesTo: Federal income tax, CPP and EI, before provincial or territorial tax

items.label: Pensionable earnings above the basic exemption
items.note: CPP is paid on earnings between the $3,500 basic exemption and the 2026 YMPE of $74,600, so on at most $71,100.

items.label: Earnings between the YMPE and YAMPE
Canada Pension Plan (CPP)
items.note: 5.95% (4.95% base plus 1% first additional) of earnings above $3,500, up to $74,600: at most $4,230.45 in 2026.

items.label: Second additional CPP (CPP2)
items.note: 4% of earnings between $74,600 and $85,000: at most $416 in 2026.

items.label: Employment Insurance (EI)
items.note: 1.63% of insurable earnings up to $68,900: at most $1,123.07 in 2026.

items.label: Base CPP contribution
items.note: The 4.95% base part of CPP earns a tax credit; the enhanced parts are deducted from income instead.

items.label: Contributions that earn a tax credit
Taxable income
items.note: Salary less the enhanced (first and second additional) CPP contributions.

items.label: Federal basic personal amount
items.note: $16,452, falling to $14,829 as taxable income rises from $181,440 to $258,482.

items.label: Federal non-refundable credits
items.note: 14% of the basic personal amount, the base CPP and EI contributions and the Canada employment amount ($1,501).

assumptions: Employment income from one job, all year, is the only income
Only the basic personal amount is claimed (TD1 claim code 1), as the CRA's payroll formulas assume
Worked out with the CRA's Payroll Deductions Formulas (T4127), so it matches tax withheld on a payslip; the return can differ
notModelled: RRSP, pension plan and union dues deductions
Credits other than the basic personal amount, CPP/EI and the Canada employment amount (e.g. spouse, dependants, tuition, medical)
The Canada Workers Benefit and other refundable credits and benefits
Provincial low-income tax reductions that are claimed on the return rather than through payroll
